description: This bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between two models—NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars)—for five different optimisation applications applied to a speech recognition system. The vertical axis lists the optimisations applied: Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates. The horizontal axis, labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper,” is a linear scale ranging from 0.000 to 0.003, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. Each optimisation has two bars, one for each model, arranged side-by-side. For the “Normalised” optimisation, the NESAC ft model shows a difference of 0.00323, while the SESHA ft model shows 0.00319. For “Add Spacing,” the NESAC ft model has a difference of 0.00319 and the SESHA ft model has 0.00311. For “Remove Spacing,” the NESAC ft model shows 0.00306 and the SESHA ft model shows 0.00299. For “Americanisms,” the NESAC ft model has a difference of 0.00302 and the SESHA ft model has 0.00257. For “Dates,” the NESAC ft model shows 0.00228 and the SESHA ft model shows 0.00228. The bars are not sorted; they are presented in the order listed on the vertical axis. The chart includes a legend indicating that orange represents the NESAC ft model and green represents the SESHA ft model.
